gloss: cooking smock; kitchen apron with sleeves

definitions.gloss: cooking smock; kitchen apron with sleeves
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese garment worn over clothes while cooking or doing housework. Unlike a Western apron, it has long sleeves and covers the torso and arms, tying at the back.

examples.japanese: {割烹着|かっぽうぎ}を{着|き}て{料理|りょうり}する。
examples.english: I cook wearing a cooking smock.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}はいつも{白|しろ}い{割烹着|かっぽうぎ}を{身|み}につけていた。
examples.english: My grandmother always wore a white cooking smock.

examples.japanese: {割烹着|かっぽうぎ}は{袖|そで}まで{覆|おお}うので、{服|ふく}が{汚|よご}れる{心配|しんぱい}がない。
examples.english: A cooking smock covers all the way to the sleeves, so there's no worry about getting your clothes dirty.

notes:
A full-coverage garment with sleeves, traditionally white, worn over a kimono or regular clothing while cooking or cleaning. Distinguished from a standard apron (エプロン) by having sleeves and wrapping around the entire upper body.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {割烹着|かっぽうぎ}を{着|き}る: to put on a cooking smock
- {割烹着|かっぽうぎ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ: to take off a cooking smock
- {白|しろ}い{割烹着|かっぽうぎ}: white cooking smock

CULTURAL NOTE:
Strongly associated with the image of a traditional Japanese homemaker or grandmother. The garment became iconic when {割烹着|かっぽうぎ} was adopted as the uniform of women's volunteer organizations during and after WWII. Today it is less commonly worn in everyday life but remains culturally recognizable.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- エプロン: apron — Western-style, typically covers only the front and has no sleeves
